customManagers.description: Track the CloudNativePG Cluster's `imageName:`. Renovate's kubernetes manager only reads `image:` keys inside pod specs, so a CNPG `Cluster.spec.imageName` is INVISIBLE to it. That is why infra-pg sat at 17.10 while the four satellite tool containers drifted to 17.11, and why Renovate then proposed 18.6 for the tools alone (#649) -- a pg_dump major skew against a live 17 server. With the Cluster tracked here and grouped by the packageRule below, the server and its tools can only move together. The optional quotes are deliberate: YAML allows `imageName: "ghcr.io/..."`, and without them the quote would be captured into depName, the datasource lookup would fail, and the Cluster would drop out of tracking with no failure signal -- the exact blind spot this manager exists to close.
Track tool versions annotated with `# renovate:` in Ansible vars (e.g. the live zot binary on the registry LXC)

packageRules.description: Keep Relay on its validated Node 22 runtime. A runtime major upgrade needs application and connector acceptance before deployment; tagless digest updates previously selected latest Node 26.
Keep Relay PostgreSQL server and dump tools on major 17. PostgreSQL 18 cannot open the existing PG17 data directory; major upgrades require a planned migration and restore rehearsal.
packageRules.groupName: relay postgres server and backup tools

packageRules.description: Do NOT track the AgentForge images in the self-hosted Zot registry. They are pinned by `just pin-workloads` / the CI pin bot, not by Renovate, and Zot garbage-collects them faster than a PR can be reviewed: on 2026-09-08 three such PRs (#540 orchestrator, #541 p1-worker, #544 sandbox) all proposed digests that already returned 404, while their CURRENT pins still resolved 200 -- so merging any of them would have pointed live workloads (five brokers, the OpenBao bootstrap Jobs, the reaper/dispatcher/worker deployments) at an unpullable image. Every PR Renovate opens for these is a 404 waiting to happen. Scoped to agentforge/* deliberately: registry.chifor.me/verdaccio digests survive fine (#545 verified 200), so the registry as a whole is still worth tracking.

The infra-pg Cluster and the four containers carrying its psql/pg_dump binaries (agentforge db-migrate, litellm wait-for-db, litellm-db-bootstrap, the infra-pg pg_dump cronjob) must move as ONE unit -- every one of those files says so in a comment, and infra-pg-dump-cronjob.yaml depends on it: a newer pg_dump can read an older server, but its output is not guaranteed to restore into that older major, so a tools-ahead-of-server bump silently invalidates the documented recovery path without failing anything. Grouping makes a split bump impossible to open; the customManager above is what lets the Cluster join the group at all. Matched by regex rather than an exact packageName so a future `postgresql-gis`-style variant, or any image the docker datasource resolves to a slightly different name, cannot silently fall outside the group and reintroduce the split bump. All five current references resolve to exactly `ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql`.
packageRules.groupName: cloudnative-pg postgresql (infra-pg cluster + its tool images)

packageRules.description: Hold ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql at 17.x. A PostgreSQL MAJOR upgrade is not an image swap: it needs a pg_upgrade of the on-disk data, a restore rehearsal against the new major, and a maintenance window -- none of which Renovate can perform or verify, and a grouped PR would look deceptively complete. #649 proposed exactly that (17.11 -> 18.6) against a live 17.10 server and was closed. 17.x minors still flow normally. Written as a regex rather than a `<18` range because this is the docker versioning scheme, where range syntax is not dependable. Lift this bound in the same change that performs the 17 -> 18 upgrade.

Digest-only bumps of MOVING tags never auto-merge. text-embeddings tracks cpu-1.9; a digest bump on it is an unreviewed upgrade of a moving tag. #899 (2026-09-27) auto-merged a digest bump of a then-tagless TEI pin onto the CUDA `latest` build and took embeddings down for hours. The `no-automerge` label makes the PR reviewbot hold these for a human; tag/version changes are unaffected. (LiteLLM left this rule when it moved to a release tag. Its own every-update `no-automerge` rule was removed on 2026-10-11, operator-directed: LiteLLM PRs now merge through the reviewers like any other update - both personas clean at the head, CI green, which for this package includes litellm-route-contract, triggered by every change to kubernetes/apps/apps/ai/litellm.yaml. That CI is the only check on a behaviour change inside the image, and it proves only what it covers: #917 was approved clean by both personas and stood with litellm-route-contract red at that head, so for this package the reviews cannot be the operative control.)

Renovate's own image (kubernetes/apps/apps/renovate/cronjob.yaml) is proposed ONCE A WEEK, and only in versions at least 3 days old. Upstream releases several times a day: 35 self-update PRs in 13 days (2026-09-28..10-11), 31% of every PR this bot opened, each paying two reviewer runs and often a re-review when a newer release moved the head mid-review (#1149). The schedule is what cuts the count - a release-age wait alone only delays every PR by 3 days, since a new release crosses the threshold on almost every 4-hourly run. The window covers the CronJob's 00:00 and 04:00 UTC runs on Monday (Renovate's timezone defaults to UTC). The age gives an upstream regression time to surface before it runs here with a write token. updateNotScheduled=false keeps an ALREADY-OPEN self-update PR inside the window too: Renovate's default keeps rebasing and re-bumping an open branch outside its schedule, so one held past Monday by a finding would still move mid-week, which is the mid-review head move (#1149) this rule exists to stop (reviewer-claude on #1272). The cost: it also suppresses CONFLICT rebases off-schedule, so a self-update PR that conflicts with main mid-week sits unmergeable until the next Monday window - that is this setting, not a bot fault. If it cannot wait, tick the rebase checkbox in that PR's description, or its entry under the Dependency Dashboard's 'Open' section (#537): Renovate honours either outside the schedule (44.150.1 branch/index.js lets rebaseRequested and a dashboard check through updateNotScheduled=false) (reviewer-claude on #1273, #1274).

The pg-sync CronJobs (kubernetes/apps/infrastructure/platform-access/pg-sync.yaml) run the CNPG operand image of the PLATFORM's strive-pg Cluster (16.9), not infra-pg's, so they must not ride the infra-pg group or its 17.x hold. #948 proposed 16.9 -> 17.11 through that group and failed CI with exit 127: the 17.11 image ships no python3, which is the CronJob's entrypoint. Held to 16.x in a group of its own; scripts/tests/test-platform-pg-sync.sh still gates every 16.x minor on python3 + psycopg2 being present. strive-pg is managed by the platform repo, so lift this bound only when that Cluster moves to 17. Must stay AFTER the two infra-pg rules above: later packageRules override earlier ones.

alpine/k8s is kubectl for in-cluster Jobs (gitea actions-run-retention, cnpg-lost-slot-reclone). kubectl is supported only within one minor of the kube-apiserver. Held to 1.34 for the 2026-10-09 program (apiserver 1.33 -> 1.34 -> 1.35; 1.34 is within one minor of all three), so the Jobs stay in skew through every hop. After the program lands on 1.35, widen to 1.34-1.36. Move this window in the same change that upgrades Kubernetes (the 1.33 upgrade missed it).

Hold the OpenBao provision-Job CLI images (quay.io/openbao/openbao) at the SERVER's minor, 2.6.x -- each Job's comment pins the CLI to the server's version. The server is the `openbao` Flux HelmRelease chart (0.29.4 = 2.6.2), and Renovate does NOT track it: the flux manager is not configured beyond its gotk-components default, so no chart PR has ever been opened. A group would therefore still produce a CLI-only bump (#938: 2.7.0 against a 2.6.2 server). Lift this bound in the same PR that bumps the chart (a human-scheduled restart of the single-replica secrets store).

Never update the S2S Phase 4 probe Job's python image (kubernetes/apps/infrastructure/s2s-phase4-probe/job.yaml), neither its tag nor its digest. It is a qualification probe, digest-pinned so that its weekly TTL re-run keeps the interpreter it was validated under, and its comment says every re-pin is deliberate. Without this rule each routine python bump for the other workloads reached it: the 3.14-slim digest refresh #1176 (opened 2026-10-09, flagged by reviewer-claude, merged 2026-10-10), the 3.15 bump #1298 (2026-10-13, probe hunk reverted by hand before merge) and #1354 (2026-10-17, the probe alone: manifests CI red and both reviewers blocking). Scoped to this one file, so every other mirror.gcr.io/library/python reference keeps its normal updates. scripts/s2s/test_phase4_job.py pins this rule (test_renovate_never_repins_the_image) next to the 3.14-slim tag (test_job_shape). A re-pin is a hand edit that re-runs those tests under the new image in the same PR.
